record.paper_title: Open problems in PDE models for knowledge-based animal movement via nonlocal perception and cognitive mapping
record.original_question: Consider the memory-smearing extension of the conflict-memory model, where populations satisfy ∂_t u_i = d_iΔu_i − γ_i∇·(u_i∇k_i g,R) and the cognitive maps satisfy ∂_t k_i = ε_iΔk_i + u_i Σ_j=1^n ρ_ij u_j − (μ + βu_i)k_i with small memory-diffusion coefficients ε_i. Under periodic boundary conditions on a bounded domain and a top-hat detection function, in what sense do time-dependent solutions exist?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 15. In what sense do solutions exist solving the time-dependent problem (2.15) subject to periodic boundary conditions and top-hat function in a bounded domain? Note that since the cognitive map equation features a diffusive term, solutions are expected to be more regular than cases without diffusion.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ with periodic boundary conditions, and an integer $n \ge 1$ of interacting populations. For each $i=1,\dots,n$ let $u_i(x,t) \ge 0$ denote the density of population $i$ and let $k_i(x,t)$ denote its cognitive map. Fix constants $d_i,\gamma_i,\varepsilon_i,\mu,\beta>0$ and a real interaction matrix $(\rho_{ij})_{i,j=1}^n$. For a perceptual radius $R>0$, define the top-hat detection function
$$g_R(z)=\frac{1}{|B_R|}\mathbf{1}_{\{|z|\le R\}},$$
and the nonlocally perceived gradient
$$\nabla \overline{k_i}^{\,g,R}(x,t) \;=\; (g_R * \nabla k_i)(x,t)\;=\;\int_\Omega g_R(x-y)\,\nabla k_i(y,t)\,dy,$$
extended periodically. Consider the coupled system
$$\partial_t u_i = d_i \Delta u_i - \gamma_i \nabla\!\cdot\!\bigl(u_i\,\nabla \overline{k_i}^{\,g,R}\bigr),$$
$$\partial_t k_i = \varepsilon_i \Delta k_i + u_i \sum_{j=1}^n \rho_{ij} u_j - (\mu + \beta u_i)k_i,$$
on $\Omega \times (0,T)$, with periodic boundary conditions for both $u_i$ and $k_i$, and with prescribed nonnegative initial data $u_i(\cdot,0)=u_i^0$, $k_i(\cdot,0)=k_i^0$. The small parameters $\varepsilon_i>0$ provide diffusive regularization of the cognitive maps.

Problem: In what functional sense (e.g. classical, strong, weak, or measure-valued) do time-dependent solutions $(u_i,k_i)_{i=1}^n$ of this system exist on $\Omega \times (0,T)$ for $T>0$? In particular, identify appropriate function spaces and assumptions on $u_i^0,k_i^0$ under which existence (and, if possible, uniqueness and regularity) of solutions can be established, exploiting the diffusive term in the $k_i$-equations to obtain regularity beyond the non-diffusive case.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent works analyze related cognitive-map PDE models (e.g., a global solvability result for a cognitive consumer-resource model with nonlocal memory usage, and bifurcation/pattern formation studies for conflict-memory and cognitive-map models with top-hat kernels), but no source clearly establishes a complete existence theory for the specific memory-smearing multi-population system with diffusive cognitive maps, periodic boundary conditions, and top-hat detection. Status appears unresolved or only partially addressed.

status_evidence.title: Global solvability and stability of cognitive consumer-resource model with nonlocal usage of memory
status_evidence.snippet: Global solvability and stability of cognitive consumer-resource model with nonlocal usage of memory
status_evidence.claim: Existence-type results have been obtained for related (but distinct) cognitive-map PDE models with nonlocal memory.

status_evidence.title: The lingering phenomenon and pattern formation in a nonlocal population model with cognitive map
status_evidence.snippet: Nonlocal population model with cognitive map; analysis of patterns and lingering phenomena
status_evidence.claim: Subsequent work focuses on bifurcation/pattern analysis rather than well-posedness of the memory-smearing extension.

status_evidence.title: Pattern Formation from Nonlocal Conflict Memory in a PDE-ODE Model
status_evidence.snippet: PDE-ODE model with nonlocal conflict memory; Hopf, Turing-Hopf, double-Hopf bifurcations with top-hat kernel
status_evidence.claim: Related conflict-memory models are studied at the level of bifurcations, not a full existence theory for the diffusive memory-smearing system.
